sentences.zh: 然后他说，噢，你经常来纽约吗？

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, all the time, which is totally a lie.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，对啊，经常来，完全是扯淡。

sentences.en: And like, I gave you like extensive notes.
sentences.zh: 而且我还给你提了大量的修改意见。

sentences.en: I was like, we're not shipping this thing.
sentences.zh: 我说，这个东西我们可不能发布。

sentences.en: It's not perfect.
sentences.zh: 它还不够完美。

sentences.en: Well, you just you never know when you might need an extra pair of socks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你就是……你永远不知道什么时候会需要多备一双袜子。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode seven, recorded on December 26, 2020.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到 ADSP 播客第七期，录制于 2020 年 12 月 26 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳。

sentences.en: And today with my co-host Bryce, we wrap up our 2020 retro.
sentences.zh: 今天我和联合主持人布莱斯一起，做我们 2020 年的年度回顾。

sentences.en: Top five counting down from five.
sentences.zh: 从第五名开始倒数前五名。

sentences.en: And we could potentially, well, one of these in particular, I mentioned to you, could be a whole, a whole episode.
sentences.zh: 我们可能……嗯，其中有一个我向你提过，它本身就能单独拿出来做整整一期节目。

sentences.en: But yeah, I'll just I'll rattle through them.

sentences.zh: 然后我们可以……我敢打赌这五个里的每一个都能单独做成一期节目，不过大概不行吧。

sentences.en: But we'll see.

sentences.en: So number five was CPPCon 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以第五名是 2020 年 CppCon 大会。

sentences.en: Definitely, you know, not not the same as, you know, being able to meet in person.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，那和能够面对面聚在一起的感觉……完全不一样。

sentences.en: But CPPCon virtual was it was still a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 但虚拟的 CppCon 依然非常有意思。

sentences.en: And we got to virtually meet online.
sentences.zh: 我们通过网络在虚拟空间相聚了。

sentences.en: I don't think you attended, but there was there was still.
sentences.zh: 我想你没参加，但现场还是……

sentences.en: No, I was there.
sentences.zh: 不，我在的。

sentences.en: I did one panel, two panels.
sentences.zh: 我参加了一个座谈会，两个座谈会。

sentences.en: I was around.
sentences.zh: 我在场来着。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，对，没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You were on a couple of the ISO committee panels.
sentences.zh: 你参加了 ISO 委员会的好几个座谈会。

sentences.en: Yeah, I didn't give a talk, but I had some panels.
sentences.zh: 对，我没有做演讲，但我参加了一些座谈会。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it was it was it was still nice to, you know, even though we couldn't in person meet virtually meet people.
sentences.zh: 对，虽然我们无法面对面，但能在线上虚拟聚会，感觉还是挺不错的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, CPPCon 2020 was my number five.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，2020 年 CppCon 是我的第五名。

sentences.en: Number four was the Prague ISO committee back in February, if I'm not mistaken.
sentences.zh: 第四名是二月份的布拉格 ISO 委员会会议，如果我没记错的话。

sentences.en: And and specifically, you know, this is not ISO related exactly, but we I don't also this could turn into a long episode again.
sentences.zh: 而且具体来说……这其实跟 ISO 没太大关系，不过我们……我也不想……这可能又变成一期很长的节目。

sentences.en: I don't I can't recall why at some point you just like a light bulb went off a year ahead and you were like, we got to make a video.
sentences.zh: 我记不清为什么在某个时刻你脑子里灵光一闪，提前一年就说，我们得拍个视频。

sentences.en: So and then we spent a day or two sort of it was primarily mostly you mostly you got to give credit.
sentences.zh: 于是我们花了一两天时间……主要大部分都是你，你得记首功。

sentences.en: Well, no.
sentences.zh: 好吧，并没有。

sentences.en: So and that's this is actually I meant to bring this question up earlier was like you mentioned sort of that we we needed to get our combined excitement out into the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，其实我刚才就想把这个问题提出来，你提到过我们需要把我们共同的激情释放到世界上。

sentences.en: You know, when was the first time that you had that thought?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你第一次有这种想法是什么时候？

sentences.en: Because potentially it was the recording of that video, because we would go and like fake interview these people.
sentences.zh: 因为有可能是在录制那个视频的时候，因为我们会去假装采访这些人。

sentences.en: And one of the best moments was when we did it with John Lakos and he had just finished his book, his new C++, you know, large scale infrastructure or architecture book.
sentences.zh: 其中最棒的时刻之一就是我们采访约翰·拉科斯（John Lakos），他刚写完他的新书，也就是他的 C++ 新书，你知道的，关于大型基础设施或架构的书。

sentences.en: And and he had a copy with him and we said, go get your go get your copy of the book.
sentences.zh: 他随身带着一本，我们说，去拿你的书来，去拿你的书。

sentences.en: And so we recorded the little bit of him holding his book.
sentences.zh: 于是我们录下了他拿着书的一小段画面。

sentences.en: And then when we cut it into the the episode, we made it look like he was just sort of constantly plugging his book, which was just hilarious.
sentences.zh: 然后当我们把它剪进这一期节目里时，我们把它处理得好像他一直在不遗余力地宣传自己的书一样，这简直太搞笑了。

sentences.en: The idea of the video was it was supposed to be both like, you know, it's supposed to show people like a slice of what the committee meeting was like and commemorate C++ 20,
sentences.zh: 这个视频的创意本来是想让人们既能看到委员会会议的一个切片，以此纪念 C++20，

sentences.en: show people what they should be excited about, but also be hilarious.
sentences.zh: 向大家展示他们应该兴奋的地方，同时又非常搞笑。

sentences.en: I recall that the idea came to me like when I was at night, like when I was sleeping and like I wrote it down on a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 我记得这个创意是在晚上冒出来的，比如我睡觉的时候，然后我把它写在了一张纸上。

sentences.en: But I think I think I felt that, you know, this was the meeting where we finalized C++ 20.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，这是我们最终敲定 C++20 的那次会议。

sentences.en: I knew C++ 20 was going to be very significant.
sentences.zh: 我知道 C++20 意义重大。

sentences.en: It was going to be the largest revision of C++ since C++ 11, you know, possibly arguably even larger.
sentences.zh: 这将是自 C++11 以来 C++ 最大的一次版本更新，你知道的，甚至可以说是史上最大的一次。

sentences.en: And I felt I always feel that I have a responsibility to help, you know,
sentences.zh: 我觉得我一直有一种责任去帮助推广我们在 C++ 上所做的所有伟大工作，

sentences.en: promote all the great work that we do on C++ and make sure that people know and are excited about what's coming.
sentences.zh: 确保人们了解即将到来的新特性并为此感到兴奋。

sentences.en: So I think it was partially that, but also partially I wanted to wanted to give people a deeper look into what the committee process was like and, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得部分原因在此，但另一方面我也想让人们更深入地了解委员会的运作流程，你知道的，

sentences.en: build more of a connection between so that like regular C++ programmers could see what the committee members were like, what the people who actually make the standard are like.
sentences.zh: 在普通 C++ 程序员和委员会成员、真正制定标准的人之间建立更多联系，让他们看到这些人的真实面貌。

sentences.en: You know, we always we do this Reddit trip report at the at the end of committee meetings.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们总是在委员会会议结束时写 Reddit 会议总结。

sentences.en: It's something that I started doing a few years ago, and it's sort of grown into this thing.
sentences.zh: 这是我几年前开始做的事情，现在已经慢慢发展成了这样一个大工程。

sentences.en: And I just sort of felt like this was like a natural extension of that.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这可以说是那项工作的自然延伸。

sentences.en: And like we should have something special for for this meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们应该为这次会议准备点特别的东西。

sentences.en: And and like, boy, that was, you know, we didn't realize that was going to be the last committee meeting we were going to have for a while.
sentences.zh: 天哪，当时我们并没有意识到那将是我们好一段时间里开的最后一次线下委员会会议。

sentences.en: But it was a really great meeting.
sentences.zh: 但那真是一次非常棒的会议。

sentences.en: It was the largest committee meeting we've had, Hannah and Avast, who hosted it, us in Prague, were really great hosts.
sentences.zh: 那是我们举办过规模最大的委员会会议，汉娜（Hannah）和阿瓦斯特（Avast）在布拉格接待了我们，他们是非常棒的东道主。

sentences.en: They were fantastic hosts.
sentences.zh: 他们是 fantastick 的东道主。（注：此处语气词保留）

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But I was I was very happy with how that video came together, that we were it was the night of the reception.
sentences.zh: 但我对这个视频的最终呈现非常满意，那是招待会当晚。

sentences.en: They threw a big reception to commemorate C++ 20.
sentences.zh: 他们举办了一场盛大的招待会来庆祝 C++20 的诞生。

sentences.en: And like we'd had I'd had this idea like a day or two days before the end of the meeting.
sentences.zh: 而这个想法是在会议结束前一两天我才想到的。

sentences.en: And like we wanted to to show the video to the committee.
sentences.zh: 我们很想把这个视频放给委员会成员看。

sentences.en: But the thing I remember most was the last day, like the closing plenary, we weren't certain whether we wanted to play the video at the end for everybody.
sentences.zh: 但我印象最深的是最后一天，也就是闭幕全体会议上，我们不确定是否要在最后为所有人播放这个视频。

sentences.en: And so we we we went up to try to play it at the end of the plenary before everybody left.
sentences.zh: 于是我们在大家离开之前，走到台上去尝试在全体会议结束时播放它。

sentences.en: And we were trying to hook it up and like we couldn't get the audio working.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图连接设备，结果却弄不好音频。

sentences.en: And there was like a two or three minute period where like people were starting to leave and like we couldn't get the audio working.
sentences.zh: 大概有两三分钟的时间，人们开始离场了，而我们还是搞不定音频。

sentences.en: And I was like, I wasn't even sure if we should be playing it there.
sentences.zh: 我当时甚至不确定我们是不是应该在那里播放它。

sentences.en: It was just sort of on a hunch that I said we should that somebody else actually, I think, said to us, you should go up and play the video.
sentences.zh: 我只是凭直觉说我们应该播放，其实是另一个人——我觉得是另一个人对我们说，你们应该上去播放这个视频。

sentences.en: We were just going to post it online and it wasn't clear whether we're going to actually be able to play it.
sentences.zh: 我们本来只打算把它发到网上，还不确定到底能不能在现场播放。

sentences.en: And then like the audio started working and we started playing it.
sentences.zh: 然后音频突然有声音了，我们开始播放视频。

sentences.en: And then like everybody just started paying attention.
sentences.zh: 接着所有人都开始关注起来。

sentences.en: Everybody came back in and they absolutely loved it.
sentences.zh: 所有人都回到了座位上，他们非常喜欢这个视频。

sentences.en: And I was I was really glad that we were able to that that worked out, that we were able to play it for everybody.
sentences.zh: 我真的很高兴我们能做到这一点，一切都很顺利，我们能为所有人播放它。

sentences.en: Because, you know, the people who work on the standard, it's sometimes it's a very thankless job.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，那些为标准工作的人，这份工作有时往往是个吃力不讨好的差事。

sentences.en: But you did an amazing job.
sentences.zh: 但你做得太棒了。

sentences.en: It was like you put that together in the span of like 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 你好像在短短 24 小时之内就把这东西给凑出来了。

sentences.en: And I don't think you slept or ate food much in that period of time.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在那期间你几乎没怎么睡觉也没怎么吃东西。

sentences.en: I ate food and I was wired on caffeine.
sentences.zh: 我吃东西了，而且我是靠咖啡因硬撑着。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I was I was up for like, I think, 48 hours or 24.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，我大概有 48 小时没睡，或者 24 小时。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was it was a long period of time that I was up for.
sentences.zh: 对，我清醒了很长很长一段时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And like I gave you like extensive notes.
sentences.zh: 而且我还给你提了大量的修改意见。

sentences.en: I was like, we're not shipping this thing.
sentences.zh: 我说，这个东西我们可不能发布。

sentences.en: It's not perfect to be to really to really explain, you know, where it's the morning of the final day.
sentences.zh: 它还不够完美——为了向大家真正解释清楚，那已经是最后一天早上了。

sentences.en: And I've at that point, you know, I've been up for, yeah, I think at least 36 hours without sleep.
sentences.zh: 到那个时候，我已经连续，对，我觉得至少有 36 小时没合眼了。

sentences.en: And I'm wired on like the whatever the prog version of Coke Zeroes are.
sentences.zh: 而且我靠着某种布拉格版本的零度可乐之类的东西强打精神。

sentences.en: I don't think they had Coke Zeroes.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们那儿没有零度可乐。

sentences.en: It was like Pepsi or something because I'm not a big coffee drinker.
sentences.zh: 好像是百事可乐之类的，因为我不怎么喝咖啡。

sentences.en: So if I need caffeine, I go to like soda.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我需要咖啡因，我就会喝苏打水。

sentences.en: And I think I have like a final draft, which has been edited heavily, like three times.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时手里拿着的是经过三次大改的最终初稿。

sentences.en: And so I've sent it to I've sent it to Bryce that morning.
sentences.zh: 我那天早上把它发给了布莱斯。

sentences.en: And and then he's still I've got to got to tweak a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 然后他还是觉得：我得再微调一下。

sentences.en: We've got to get rid of the, you know, this logo.
sentences.zh: 我们得把这个……你知道的，这个标志去掉。

sentences.en: And so, yes, it's you got a lot of credits on the executive producer, executive editor, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，你在演职员表里挂了很多头衔，执行制片人、执行总监等等等等。

sentences.en: We'll link it in the in the show notes for those that haven't seen.
sentences.zh: 我们会在节目简介里附上链接，还没看过的朋友可以去看看。

sentences.en: And then afterwards, we had a bet and I don't remember the specifics of the bet, but we had some crazy bet on how many views the video would get was going to get.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我们打了个赌，我不记得赌局的具体细节了，但我们针对这个视频能获得多少播放量打了一个疯狂的赌。

sentences.en: And then I had a hedge on the bet where I had a separate bet with another person about how few videos the views the video would get.
sentences.zh: 然后我还给这个赌买了个保险，我和另一个人私下又打了个赌，赌这个视频的播放量会少到什么程度。

sentences.en: I think the bet involved you buying like whoever won the bet between me and you had to take the other one to a very fancy sushi restaurant in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我记得赌注是如果你我之间谁赢了，输的一方得请赢家去旧金山一家非常高档的寿司店吃饭。

sentences.en: And I recall that I lost that bet and I still owe you that like that very expensive sushi dinner.
sentences.zh: 我记得我输了那个赌局，而且我到现在还欠着你那顿非常昂贵的寿司大餐。

sentences.en: Yeah, it got I can't remember the video got in the in the time slot that we had set the bet for.
sentences.zh: 对，在我们在赌局里设定的时间段内，我记不清视频具体拿到了多少播放量。

sentences.en: I think it got like 20 or 30,000 views.
sentences.zh: 我想大概拿到了两三万次播放吧。

sentences.en: But I think the bet was that it had to be at the time my most viewed video, which was like 60,000 views or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但当时的赌局要求是它必须达到我所有视频中播放量最高的一次，大概是 6 万次播放左右。

sentences.en: So it came close, but it did not it did not make the cut, which was fine for me.
sentences.zh: 所以它差了一点，但没有达到要求，这对我来说倒也无所谓。

sentences.en: I get some free sushi.
sentences.zh: 我能白蹭一顿寿司。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was it was there was there was there was some combination of the bet out of the of the outcome, the multiple bets that involved me having to having to get a mohawk.
sentences.zh: 对，那里面包含了一系列赌局结果的组合，由于这几个不同的赌局，导致我最后不得不去留一个莫霍克发型。

sentences.en: And I was just glad that that that outcome did not happen.
sentences.zh: 我只是很高兴最后那个结果没有发生。

sentences.en: But yes, so that was that was number four.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，这就是第四名。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: We got to I said I was going to lightning lightning round these and have not been lightning running them.
sentences.zh: 我们得……我说过我要开启闪电连击模式，结果一点也没闪电起来。

sentences.en: So, yeah, number five was CBP con 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，第五名是 CppCon 2020。

sentences.en: Number four was the prog and the filming and sort of editing of that video and getting to interview folks.
sentences.zh: 第四名是布拉格之旅、拍摄和剪辑那个视频以及采访大家的过程。

sentences.en: That was that was a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 那真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: Number three is starting this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 第三名是创办这个播客。

sentences.en: I don't think we have to say much about that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个我们不用多说什么。

sentences.en: This has been a blaSt.
sentences.zh: 这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It would probably be higher on the list if we had more than five or six episodes.
sentences.zh: 如果我们播出的期数不止五六期的话，它在榜单上的排名可能会更高。

sentences.en: But yeah, this is sort of we just started at this tail end of the year.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，我们是在今年年底才刚开始做这个。

sentences.en: Number two, this is the one that I really think could be a whole episode.
sentences.zh: 第二名，这个是我真心觉得可以单独特地做成一整期节目的事情。

sentences.en: Before COVID had really taken off at the end of February, this was the last time I did anything.
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情于二月底真正爆发之前，这是我做的最后一件事。

sentences.en: I had booked a flight down to New York and I spent two or three days with Arthur Whitney,
sentences.zh: 我订了一张去纽约的机票，和阿瑟·惠特尼（Arthur Whitney）一起度了两三天，

sentences.en: who is probably a name you've never heard of and a name that many listeners of this podcast have never heard of.
sentences.zh: 他可能是一个你从未听过的名字，也是本播客许多听众从未听过的名字。

sentences.en: Arthur Whitney is Kenneth Iverson's protégé, which is like enter the whole other podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 阿瑟·惠特尼是肯尼斯·艾佛森（Kenneth Iverson）的门徒，这完全可以展开说另一期播客了。

sentences.en: So Kenneth Iverson, for those that have not remembered from the past episodes, is the inventor of APL and the creator of APL.
sentences.zh: 所以肯尼斯·艾佛森，如果大家从过往节目中还没忘记的话，就是 APL 语言的发明者和创造者。

sentences.en: And he had a protégé that went on to invent a language called K.
sentences.zh: 而他的一个门徒后来发明了一种名为 K 的语言。

sentences.en: And there's been eight different versions of that.
sentences.zh: 这种语言已经有过八个不同的版本了。

sentences.en: And then K spawned sort of two other languages.
sentences.zh: 然后 K 语言衍生出了另外两种语言。

sentences.en: The most recent version of it is Shakti.
sentences.zh: 它的最新版本是 Shakti。

sentences.en: And then Q is a descendant of K, specifically from K4.
sentences.zh: 而 Q 语言是 K 的后代，具体来说源自 K4。

sentences.en: I had sent him an email about having a phone call to chat.
sentences.zh: 我曾给他发过一封邮件，询问能否通个电话聊聊。

sentences.en: And then he was like, oh, do you ever come to New York?
sentences.zh: 然后他说，噢，你经常来纽约吗？

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, all the time, which is totally a lie.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，对啊，经常来，完全是扯淡。

sentences.en: And then I spent a couple days, yeah, not for eight hours a day chatting with him, but we had dinner and we talked a few times.
sentences.zh: 接着我花了几呆……对，不是每天跟他聊八个小时，但我们一起吃了晚饭，聊了好几次。

sentences.en: And his story is absolutely phenomenal and will be a part of the APL talk that I give in the future.
sentences.zh: 他的故事绝对堪称传奇，也将成为我以后关于 APL 的演讲的一部分。

sentences.en: And the number one is starting the Programming Languages Virtual Meetup that I started back in May as sort of something to give myself to do and also to hold myself accountable when reading books and stuff.
sentences.zh: 而第一名是创办了我在五月份发起“编程语言虚拟聚会”，当时是为了给自己找点事做，也是为了在阅读书籍等内容时监督自己。

sentences.en: And we've been working our way through the structure and interpretation of computer prograMs.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在通读《计算机程序的构造和解释》（SICP）。

sentences.en: And that has just been – it's been a blast the same way that this podcast has.
sentences.zh: 那段经历——就和这个播客一样，简直太棒了。

sentences.en: There's a core group of individuals that we meet on Mondays and we're at the tail end of chapter – we're on chapter 5.3 and it goes to 5.5.
sentences.zh: 我们有一群核心成员在每周一聚会，我们目前快读完这一章了——我们在读 5.3 节，总共有 5.5 节。

sentences.en: So we're almost done.
sentences.zh: 所以我们快要完成了。

sentences.en: And, yeah, meeting with that group of folks just like virtually in the pandemic has been awesome because, yeah, we don't really get to go to meetups in person anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且，在疫情期间和这群人在虚拟空间聚会感觉太棒了，因为，对，我们真的没法再线下参加聚会了。

sentences.en: So it's nice to be able to chat with folks virtually and, yeah, that's my top five liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以能在线上和大家聊天真的很美好，对，这就是我的前五名榜单。

sentences.en: Didn't you also start at NVIDIA this year?
sentences.zh: 你不是今年也加入了英伟达吗？

sentences.en: When did you start at NVIDIA?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候加入英伟达的？

sentences.en: I started – so that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 我是……所以这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: I actually – there was a couple things that I was like, oh, that's top of the list for sure.
sentences.zh: 我其实……有几件事我当时觉得，噢，这绝对稳居榜首。

sentences.en: And then I realized that that was – those things happened in 2019.
sentences.zh: 然后我才意识到那是——那些事情发生在 2019 年。

sentences.en: So I started in NVIDIA at October 2019.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在 2019 年 10 月加入英伟达的。

sentences.en: We could do – well, so the one thing that I thought, oh, yeah, that's number one for sure and then realized it was – 2019 was our Belfast dinner,
sentences.zh: 我们可以——嗯，所以我认为的一件事是，“哦，对，那绝对是第一名”，然后才意识到那是——2019 年我们在贝尔法斯特的晚宴，

sentences.en: which I'm sure you have very fond memories.
sentences.zh: 我相信你对那次晚宴有着非常美好的回忆。

sentences.en: Oh, I remember that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我记得那个。

sentences.en: That will forever be like one of my career and life highlights.
sentences.zh: 那将永远是我职业生涯和生活中的高光时刻之一。

sentences.en: Good times.
sentences.zh: 美好的时光。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was – it was a – That whole – that whole – the whole fall of 2019 where we spent more time at conferences than we did at, like, our home, that was good.
sentences.zh: 对，那是——那是一个——整个——整个2019年的秋天，我们花在会议上的时间比花在家里还要多，那真的很棒。

sentences.en: That was a good – that was a good period.
sentences.zh: 那是一段美好的——那是一段美好的时期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Fun trivia fact.
sentences.zh: 一个有趣的冷知识。

sentences.en: So on the – on our, like, little banner photo on our Twitter profile is – now there's a photo of us at the Scrabble game.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的——在我们的推特个人资料的小横幅照片上——现在有一张我们在玩《拼字游戏》的照片。

sentences.en: But the original photo, which is still there off to the side, is a picture of Bryce and I under – oh, I'm not going to remember the park off the top of my head.
sentences.zh: 但原图（旁边其实还能看到）是一张我和布莱斯在——哦，我一下子想不起那是哪个公园了。

sentences.en: My sister will be disappointed, but she doesn't listen to this podcast, so that's fine.
sentences.zh: 我妹妹会失望的，不过她不听这个播客，所以没关系。

sentences.en: And we were at a park in Dublin because Bryce and I – well, I had gone to visit my sister who lives in Dublin, one of my three sisters that lives in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 我们在都柏林的一个公园，因为我和布莱斯——好吧，我去探望住在都柏林的妹妹，我住在都柏林的三个妹妹之一。

sentences.en: And I went to help.
sentences.zh: 然后我去帮忙。

sentences.en: And Bryce invited himself.
sentences.zh: 结果布莱斯不请自来。

sentences.en: And then we went to this park and we saw some deer and Bryce brought extra shoes and socks because apparently that's what Bryce does and I did not.
sentences.zh: 然后我们去了这个公园，看到了一些鹿，布莱斯带了备用的鞋子和袜子，因为显然布莱斯就是这样的人，而我没有。

sentences.en: I brought extra shoes and socks and you did not and whose feet were very cold on the bus ride back to BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 我带了备用鞋子和袜子，而你没有，结果在坐大巴回贝尔法斯特的路上，谁的脚超级冷？

sentences.en: Mine were.
sentences.zh: 我的。

sentences.en: I just – you just – I just remember walking through, like, this marshy park and then afterwards you just whip out this new pair of socks and shit.
sentences.zh: 我只是——你只是——我只记得走过这样一个泥泞的公园，然后事后你竟然掏出一双崭新的袜子换上。

sentences.en: I'm just like, who does this?
sentences.zh: 我就想，谁会这样做？

sentences.en: Well, you just – you never know when you might need an extra pair of socks.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你就是——你永远不知道什么时候会需要一双备用袜子。

sentences.en: Got to learn to travel.
sentences.zh: 得学会旅行。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, let's see.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对，让我想想。

sentences.en: My top – well, okay, I got a liSt.
sentences.zh: 我的榜单——好吧，好吧，我有个清单。

sentences.en: It's unordered and it may or may not be five things.
sentences.zh: 它是无序的，里面可能刚好有五件事，也可能没有。

sentences.en: So obviously, you know, pretty high up there is the fact that we published C++20, which is, I'm going to say, the most impactful revision of C++ and C++11 at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，你知道的，排在比较靠前的是我们发布了C++20，我认为这是自C++11以来最具影响力的C++版本。

sentences.en: So we finalized it at the Prague meeting in February and then it went through all the various stages of publication and it was officially published by ISO like a week or so ago.
sentences.zh: 我们在2月份的布拉格会议上敲定了它，然后它经历了出版的各个阶段，大概在一周前被ISO正式发布了。

sentences.en: So – and there's some other C++ things.
sentences.zh: 所以——还有一些其他关于C++的事情。

sentences.en: So at the Prague meeting, Titus Winters, who had been the library evolution chair on the C++ committee – that library evolution is basically the library design group.
sentences.zh: 所以在布拉格会议上，蒂图斯·温特斯（Titus Winters）曾担任C++委员会的库演进主席——库演进基本上就是库设计小组。

sentences.en: And it was an interesting time to take on the job because we had this plan for where there was going to be a transition period and then that all got scrapped by the fact that the pandemic hit and we didn't have a summer meeting or a fall meeting.
sentences.zh: 接手这份工作是一个很有趣的时期，因为我们原本有一个过渡期的计划，但由于疫情爆发，我们既没有夏季会议也没有秋季会议，这个计划全部泡汤了。

sentences.en: So it was sort of a trial by fire and I'm very, very grateful that Herb Sutter had the wisdom to suggest that, you know, maybe chairing shouldn't just be, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是烈火中的考验，我非常非常感谢赫b·萨特（Herb Sutter）的智慧，他建议说，你知道的，也许主席不应该只是……

sentences.en: a one-person thing.
sentences.zh: 由一个人担任。

sentences.en: And so he suggested, well, you should have a co-chair, a vice chair, Fabio.
sentences.zh: 所以他建议，法比奥，你应该有一个联合主席、一个副主席。

sentences.en: And then I sort of took that to the extreme where I recruited another vice chair and then I brought on some other people to help.
sentences.zh: 然后我把这个想法发挥到了极致，招募了另一个副主席，还找了其他人来帮忙。

sentences.en: And so now we have this whole, like, library evolution leadership team, which is great because we get to spread the load, makes us a lot more effective.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了整个库演进领导团队，这太棒了，因为我们可以分担工作量，这让我们高效得多。

sentences.en: So I've been very – I think that's the best thing that we've done in library evolution has been this notion of not just having one person in charge but having a leadership team.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直非常——我认为我们在库演进中所做的最好的一件事就是这种理念：不只是让一个人负责，而是拥有一个领导团队。

sentences.en: And there was also some exciting stuff that we did at NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 我们在英伟达也做了一些令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: So we launched the NVIDIA HPC SDK, which I work on.
sentences.zh: 我们推出了英伟达HPC SDK，这也是我参与的项目。

sentences.en: We launched NVIDIA C++, which is our new C++ compiler that has some very cool features like GPU-accelerated C++ parallel algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 我们推出了英伟达C++，这是我们全新的C++编译器，它有一些非常酷的功能，比如GPU加速的C++并行算法。

sentences.en: It's kind of funny.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: Before I was at NVIDIA, I was at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, and one of the main things I was working on there was getting the C++ parallel algorithms into C++.
sentences.zh: 在加入英伟达之前，我在劳伦斯伯克利国家实验室工作，我在那里主要负责的工作之一就是将C++并行算法引入C++标准中。

sentences.en: And so I was working on writing the spec, and then I left Lawrence – and then the spec got in.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时在编写规范，然后我离开了劳伦斯——接着规范被采纳了。

sentences.en: Then I left Lawrence Berkeley, and I went to NVIDIA where my, like, first job was, like, hey, go implement this spec.
sentences.zh: 然后我离开劳伦斯伯克利，加入了英伟达，我的第一份工作居然是，嘿，去实现这个规范。

sentences.en: So I got to write the spec.
sentences.zh: 所以我先写了规范。

sentences.en: I then got paid to implement.
sentences.zh: 然后我又拿到了实现它的薪水。

sentences.en: And my team also shipped our heterogeneous C++ standard library this year, the first release of that.
sentences.zh: 我的团队今年还发布了我们的异构C++标准库，这是它的第一个版本。

sentences.en: And, yeah, I think that's pretty much it.
sentences.zh: 对，我想差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: Oh, and we – you know, my team sort of, like, doubled in size, which has been pretty exciting.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有我们——你知道的，我的团队规模差不多翻了一番，这非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: We've hired some pretty awesome people.
sentences.zh: 我们招募了一些非常棒的人。

sentences.en: We've now got a really great team working on all of our open source libraries, and I'm really proud of all the work they're doing.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有了一支非常优秀的团队来负责我们所有的开源库，我为他们所做的工作感到无比骄傲。

sentences.en: Yeah, NVIDIA is – we sort of have alluded to this before on past episodes, but we more and more are headed in the direction of becoming an open source company, which,
sentences.zh: 对，英伟达——我们在过去的节目中也曾暗示过这一点，但我们正越来越多地朝成为一家开源公司的方向发展，而正如你所说……

sentences.en: as you have remarked, is not historically what NVIDIA is known for.
sentences.zh: 这在历史上并不是英伟达的作风。

sentences.en: Yeah, but you and I both work at parts of the company where we pretty much exclusively work on open source stuff.
sentences.zh: 是的，但你和我都在公司里几乎专门从事开源工作的部分工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, which is – I absolutely love it.
sentences.zh: 对，这一点——我简直爱死它了。

sentences.en: I mean, there's many, many reasons it's awesome, but one of the reasons is I can just – I can talk about everything I do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它很棒的原因有很多很多，其中之一就是我可以——我可以谈论我做的所有事情。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, you can go and look at my commits and what I do for work and what I get paid for.
sentences.zh: 比如，你可以去查看我的提交记录，看看我为工作做了什么，以及我拿着薪水在做什么。

sentences.en: So if I wanted to start – you know, if I wanted to start Twitch streaming my day job, I technically could do that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我想开始——你知道的，如果我想在Twitch上直播我的日常工作，从技术上讲我是可以做到的。

sentences.en: I'm not sure how my picks would feel about it, but if I wanted to become, you know, a Twitch streamer and just, you know, stream my work, I think that would be totally okay.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我的领导们会怎么想，但如果我真的想成为一名Twitch主播，然后仅仅直播我的工作，我认为这完全没问题。

sentences.en: Well, don't worry.
sentences.zh: 好吧，别担心。

sentences.en: None of your picks have enough time to have listened through to the end of this episode.
sentences.zh: 你们没有哪个领导有闲心把这期节目从头到尾听完。

sentences.en: But that's true.
sentences.zh: 不过倒也是实话。

sentences.en: They've got much better things to do.
sentences.zh: 他们有更有意义的事情要做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: All of that being said – So what are you excited about for next year?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此——那么，你对明年有什么期待？

sentences.en: What are you looking forward to in 2021?
sentences.zh: 你对2021年有什么展望？

sentences.en: Well, I have a document, a sort of goals document.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我有一个文档，一个类似目标清单的文档。

sentences.en: Of course you do.
sentences.zh: 你当然有。

sentences.en: Of course you do.
sentences.zh: 你当然有。

sentences.en: And there's a section within my document of broad categories, which has seven bullet points or six.
sentences.zh: 我的文档里有一个关于宏观分类的章节，里面有七个要点，或者六个。

sentences.en: Some of them can't be talked about.
sentences.zh: 其中有些是不能公开谈论的。

sentences.en: But, yes, so Meetup is one of them to continue to do that.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，读书会是其中之一，我们会继续办下去。

sentences.en: So we're wrapping up structure and interpretation of computer programs, and we'll either be starting concepts and techniques –
sentences.zh: 所以我们即将完成《计算机程序的构造和解释》的研读，接下来我们要么开始《概念与技术》——

sentences.en: or CTM, whatever that stands for, concepts, techniques of modeling for computer prograMs.
sentences.zh: 或者叫CTM，不管它全称是什么，计算机程序建模的概念与技术。

sentences.en: Then, obviously, you know, my day job is awesome and going to be continuing to work on QDF, which is the GPU version of Pandas, which is –
sentences.zh: 然后，很显然，你知道的，我的日常工作非常棒，而且会继续开发QDF，也就是Pandas的GPU版本，这——

sentences.en: It's honestly – it's the story of how I sort of landed there, quasi-thanks to you, and then how I have post-landing on this team at NVIDIA have fallen in love with APL.
sentences.zh: 老实说——这就是我如何来到这里的过程，多亏了你，以及自从加入英伟达这个团队后，我是如何爱上APL的。

sentences.en: It is a very, very fortuitous thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常非常幸运的事。

sentences.en: I won't go into the details, but basically QDF and Pandas are essentially descendants of APL.
sentences.zh: 我就不展开细节了，但基本上QDF和Pandas本质上都是APL的后代。

sentences.en: It's – not many people are aware of that, but APL – APL, one of the children languages is J.
sentences.zh: 这——没多少人知道这一点，但是APL的子语言之一是J。

sentences.en: J influenced Wes McKinney when he was at AQR, who is the author of Pandas, and then Pandas has basically inspired QDF.
sentences.zh: J语言启发了当时在AQR的韦斯·麦金尼（Wes McKinney），他正是Pandas的作者，而Pandas基本上又启发了QDF。

sentences.en: So these – it all leads back to – everything leads back to APL.
sentences.zh: 所以这些——一切都可以追溯到——万物皆可追溯到APL。

sentences.en: Take a shot at eggnog.
sentences.zh: 来杯蛋奶酒庆祝一下。

sentences.en: But – and then, yeah, this podcast, there's a bunch of projects that I want to work on.
sentences.zh: 不过——对，这个播客，还有一堆我想做的项目。

sentences.en: Talks are going to – I'm probably going to try and give less talks this year because it took up a lot.
sentences.zh: 演讲方面——我今年可能会尽量少做一些演讲，因为这占用了太多时间。

sentences.en: That's funny.
sentences.zh: 真搞笑。

sentences.en: I'm probably going to give more talks this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年可能会做更多演讲。

sentences.en: I didn't give a lot of talks this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年没做太多演讲。

sentences.en: I was like, you know what?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm at home, pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我在家里，碰上大流行。

sentences.en: I can be a little bit lazy.
sentences.zh: 我可以稍微偷懒一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was – I gave a lot of talks last year and also, too, a lot of, like, unique talks, meaning I didn't give the same talk repeatedly,
sentences.zh: 对，我——我去年做了很多演讲，而且有很多都是独特的演讲，意思是我没有反复做同一个演讲。

sentences.en: which probably would have been – would have saved me – wouldn't have caused as much work.
sentences.zh: 那样做的话可能会——会省点事——就不会引起那么多工作量了。

sentences.en: It was awesome, but I think I'm just a little burnt out on giving talks.
sentences.zh: 这很棒，但我觉得我对做演讲有点职业倦怠了。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that will change in two weeks, and then I'll want to give another one.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定两周后这想法就会变，然后我又想再做一个了。

sentences.en: And then also, yeah, ISO C++ ranges involved there.
sentences.zh: 然后还有，对，涉及ISO C++ ranges（范围库）。

sentences.en: And then potentially, yeah, depending on what's getting prioritized, there could be some other ISO C++ stuff.
sentences.zh: 接着可能还有，这取决于优先级的安排，可能会有一些其他的ISO C++相关事务。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's a lot of stuff, a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，有很多事情，非常多。

sentences.en: What are you excited about?
sentences.zh: 你对什么感到兴奋？

sentences.en: I think the things that I'm most excited about I can't say anything about for the next two to three months, but I'm going to be giving some talks,
sentences.zh: 我觉得最让我兴奋的事情在接下来两三个月内我还无可奉告，但我会做一些演讲，

sentences.en: announcing some exciting stuff at NVIDIA's conference this year.
sentences.zh: 在英伟达今年的会议上宣布一些令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: But in terms of things that I can talk about, this is sort of the year where we'll finalize features for C++ 23.
sentences.zh: 但就我能公开的内容而言，今年将是我们敲定C++23特性的年份。

sentences.en: Now, that sounds maybe a little surprising because, like, isn't 23 a few years away?
sentences.zh: 听起来可能有点让人惊讶，因为，23不还是好几年后的事吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, we have to do all of the design work pretty early on the major features so that we can then work out all the bugs.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我们必须在早期对主要特性进行所有的设计工作，这样我们才能随后解决所有的漏洞。

sentences.en: So, by the end of this year, you know, it'll be the end of 2021, and we want to have all of the major features together because sometime in 2022,
sentences.zh: 所以，到今年年底，也就是2021年底，我们希望把所有的主要特性都整合在一起，因为在2022年的某个时候，

sentences.en: we want to send out a committee draft of the standard where we can get a bunch of feedback and identify any bugs in it.
sentences.zh: 我们想要发布一份标准的委员会草案，以便收集大量反馈并找出其中的任何漏洞。

sentences.en: So, we really need to, by the end of this year, by this time next year, have finalized all of the major library features.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们真的需要在今年年底，也就是明年的这个时候，敲定所有主要的库特性。

sentences.en: The two big ones that we're working on are C++ executors, which is an abstraction for expressing parallel work to be executed and dependencies and chains and graphs of work
sentences.zh: 我们在做的两个大项目是C++执行器（Executors），它是一种用于表达要执行的并行工作、依赖关系以及工作链和图的抽象，

sentences.en: and separating that away from what particular type of resource is going to run that work.
sentences.zh: 并将这些与运行这些工作的具体资源类型隔离开来。

sentences.en: And then the other big thing that's in the pipeline is the C++ networking proposal.
sentences.zh: 另一个正在推进的大项目是C++网络提案（Networking proposal）。

sentences.en: And then we also have a goal of trying to come up with a plan for what a modular standard library will look like in landing library support for co-routines.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们的目标还包括：为模块化标准库制定一个规划方案，并着手将协程（co-routines）的库支持落地。

sentences.en: I'm not certain that we'll be able to achieve all those goals.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我们是否能实现所有这些目标。

sentences.en: You know, COVID has slowed down our progress a bit, but I'm fairly hopeful that we'll be able to at least land executors and, if not, land it in 2023,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，新冠疫情在一定程度上放慢了我们的进度，但我相当有希望我们至少能落地执行器；如果不能在2023年落地，

sentences.en: that we'll be able to put out, at the very least, a technical specification in 2022 or 2023.
sentences.zh: 我们至少能在2022年或2023年发布一份技术规范。

sentences.en: So, I think that's probably the work that I'm most excited about in the standards world for the next year.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这可能是标准委员会世界里，我在接下来的一年中最期待的工作。

sentences.en: And, yeah, I think that's pretty much it.
sentences.zh: 好了，差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: There's some other things, but as I said, I can't spoil the secret quite yet.
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些事情，但正如我所说，我还不能剧透。

sentences.en: There's several things we can't talk about, but in the future, all will be revealed.
sentences.zh: 有几件事我们不能谈论，但在未来，一切都会水落石出。

sentences.en: And, yeah, it's an exciting time, you know, in the midst of working remotely and not being able to meet in person.
sentences.zh: 而且，在这个需要远程办公、无法进行线下会面的时期，这确实是一个激动人心的时刻。

sentences.en: It's still awesome that, you know, there's great work being done, you know, on our day-to-day jobs at NVIDIA, but also sort of in the broader scope of C++ and the ISO committee.
sentences.zh: 令人惊叹的是，我们在英伟达的日常工作中，以及在更广泛的C++和ISO委员会的视野中，仍然取得了伟大的成果。

sentences.en: And then also, whether it's meetups or podcasts, a lot of podcasts that are coming out.
sentences.zh: 然后还有，无论是读书会还是播客，都有很多新播客涌现出来。

sentences.en: I don't know what happened, but now there's been –
sentences.zh: 我不知道发生了什么，但现在已经有了——

sentences.en: Well, we started a podcast and everybody wanted to, you know, be like us.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们开启了一个播客，然后每个人都想——你知道的，想像我们一样。

sentences.en: Can we say that?
sentences.zh: 我们能这么说吗？

sentences.en: We weren't actually technically, I think, too much to your –
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，我们其实——我觉得这不太符合你的——

sentences.en: JF and Chris retroactively copied our idea.
sentences.zh: JF和克里斯（Chris）是追溯性地抄袭了我们的创意。

sentences.en: How did they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Time travel.
sentences.zh: 时间旅行。

sentences.en: Time travel.
sentences.zh: 时间旅行。

sentences.en: So they –
sentences.zh: 所以他们——

sentences.en: The only way that they got their episode out first was because of time travel?
sentences.zh: 他们能率先发布那一集唯一的可能是因为时间旅行？

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: So we were the first of the new podcasts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是这批新播客里的鼻祖。

sentences.en: That is right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, see, and like I said, I learn something every episode.
sentences.zh: 你看，就像我说的，我每一集都能学到新东西。

sentences.en: We'll link the – so for those that don't know, so there's JF and Chris's podcast, TLB Hit.
sentences.zh: 我们会把链接放上——所以对于那些不知道的人来说，这里有JF和克里斯的播客《TLB Hit》。

sentences.en: NDR, No Diagnostic Required, is a new C++ news-focused podcaSt.
sentences.zh: NDR（No Diagnostic Required）是一个专注于C++新闻的新播客。

sentences.en: I didn't even know about that one.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都不知道这个。

sentences.en: I learned something new.
sentences.zh: 我又学到了新东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So there's now –
sentences.zh: 所以现在有了——

sentences.en: Who's running that one?
sentences.zh: 谁在主持那个？

sentences.en: That's Anastasia Kosakawa.
sentences.zh: 那是阿纳斯塔西娅·小川（Anastasia Kosakawa）。

sentences.en: I'm probably pronouncing that last name incorrectly.
sentences.zh: 我可能把这个姓氏读错了。

sentences.en: And then Phil Nash of JetBrains.
sentences.zh: 还有来自JetBrains的菲尔·纳什（Phil Nash）。

sentences.en: So it's one of the JetBrains podcasts.
sentences.zh: 所以这是JetBrains的系列播客之一。

sentences.en: They have a bunch of them.
sentences.zh: 他们有一堆这样的播客。

sentences.en: I got to give JetBrains a shout-out.
sentences.zh: 我得给JetBrains点个赞。

sentences.en: I was recently – I needed to answer a question about like the C++ community.
sentences.zh: 我最近——我需要回答一个关于C++社区的问题。

sentences.en: It was about like what build systems and IDEs are popular.
sentences.zh: 内容大概是关于哪些构建系统和集成开发环境（IDE）比较受欢迎。

sentences.en: And I was able to use the JetBrains developer ecosystem survey to like get that answer for like the past like three or four years.
sentences.zh: 我能够利用 JetBrains 开发者生态系统调查来获取过去三四年来类似这样的答案。

sentences.en: Like they do – JetBrains does every year this very impressive and like professionally done survey of developer ecosystems in the C++ community.
sentences.zh: 就像他们所做的那样——JetBrains 每年都会在 C++ 社区中进行这项非常令人印象深刻且专业制作的开发者生态系统调查。

sentences.en: And then they like publish all the results.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会把所有结果公布出来。

sentences.en: Like they could just have chosen not to do that and just been like, yeah, we'll pay this money, we'll put the survey together, and then we'll just – you know,
sentences.zh: 比如他们本来完全可以选择不这么做，直接说，行吧，我们出这笔钱，把调查做出来，然后——你知道的，

sentences.en: we're not going to share it with anybody because why would we?
sentences.zh: 我们不打算跟任何人分享，因为我们为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: It's like this thing that we spent resources on.
sentences.zh: 这毕竟是我们投入了资源的东西。

sentences.en: But no, they like publish it, which I think is super awesome.
sentences.zh: 但没有，他们还是将其公开发布了，我觉得这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: So a big shout-out to JetBrains for that.
sentences.zh: 所以要对 JetBrains 表示大大的感谢。

sentences.en: The survey is – it's called the JetBrains Developer Ecosystem Survey.
sentences.zh: 这项调查——它被称为 JetBrains 开发者生态系统调查。

sentences.en: And I think it's got some really useful data in it.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为其中包含了一些非常有用的大数据。

sentences.en: Not only do they publish all the data, they also publish their methodology.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅公开了所有数据，还公开了他们的调查方法。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's very clear that they didn't just have somebody go and throw together a SurveyMonkey survey and distribute it to a bunch of people.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可以看出，很显然他们并不是随便找个人弄个 SurveyMonkey 问卷调查就发给一大群人了事。

sentences.en: Like they put some thought into this.
sentences.zh: 可以看出他们是动了一番脑筋的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I'll definitely link that in the show notes as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我肯定也会把这个链接放到节目笔记中。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think now technically there are, at least on my radar, three C++ specific.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，我觉得现在从技术上讲，至少在我的雷达范围内，有三个专注于 C++ 的播客。

sentences.en: There's the CppCast, CppChat, and NDr.
sentences.zh: 有 CppCast、CppChat 以及 NDr。

sentences.en: And then there's now this, like, second layer of, like, developers in the C++ ecosystem that have launched their different flavors of podcasts, which is TLB Hit, our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后现在又有了第二层的 C++ 生态系统开发者，他们推出了自己不同风格的播客，也就是 TLB Hit，也就是我们的播客。

sentences.en: And now the new podcast that I just listened to, the episode zero last night, was the Two's Compliment podcast,
sentences.zh: 而现在我昨晚刚听了第零集的新播客是 Two's Compliment 播客，

sentences.en: which is hosted by Matt Gobolt of Compiler Explorer and an individual who I was not familiar with, Ben Rady,
sentences.zh: 它由 Compiler Explorer 的 Matt Gobolt 以及一位我不太熟悉的人 Ben Rady 共同主持，

sentences.en: who I think has given a bunch of – at least it sounds like from episode zero – a bunch of talks on testing.
sentences.zh: 我想他做过很多——听第零集的感觉是，他做过很多关于测试的演讲。

sentences.en: And there's – I can't actually tell what their – the theme of their website is, like, game development.
sentences.zh: 而且我——其实我看不出他们的网站主题是什么，比如是游戏开发吗？

sentences.en: Sort of looks like a retro arcade.
sentences.zh: 看起来有点像复古街机。

sentences.en: But their whole first episode was on testing.
sentences.zh: 但他们的第一期节目讲的完全是测试。

sentences.en: So I'm not sure if it's going to be sort of random musings like ours is where it's just them talking about whatever they want or if it's going to be game-focused.
sentences.zh: 所以我不太确定它会像我们这样是那种随性的闲聊，即兴谈论他们想谈的任何话题，还是会专注于游戏领域。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I love podcasts.
sentences.zh: 不过，我是说，我太喜欢播客了。

sentences.en: So the more podcasts, the better, the merrier.
sentences.zh: 所以播客越多越好，越多越热闹。

sentences.en: It kind of reminds me of, like, you know, a few years ago there were just, like, two C++ conferences, C++ Now – oh, sorry, three C++ conferences, C++ Now, CppCon, and Meaning C++.
sentences.zh: 这有点让我想起，你知道的，几年前只有大约两个 C++ 会议，C++ Now——哦，抱歉，三个 C++ 会议，C++ Now、CppCon 和 Meeting C++。

sentences.en: And then suddenly there was an explosion.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间就迎来了大爆发。

sentences.en: Same thing's happening with podcasts.
sentences.zh: 播客现在也正在经历同样的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's – there's another thing to be very, very grateful for, you know, in our 2020 retro slash Fortran episode is that as C++ developers,
sentences.zh: 对，这也是——在我们的 2020 年复古兼 Fortran 特别节目中，还有一件事让我们非常非常感激，那就是作为 C++ 开发者，

sentences.en: we are absolutely spoiled with content in the form of conference talks and podcasts.
sentences.zh: 我们在会议演讲和播客形式的内容方面简直是被宠坏了。

sentences.en: Like, as much as I am an APL fan, there is not a cornucopia of, like, APL talks and podcasts that I can go listen to and, like, pick my favorite.
sentences.zh: 就像，尽管我是一个 APL 的粉丝，但并没有海量的 APL 演讲和播客可供我去聆听并挑选出我最喜欢的。

sentences.en: There's not even a single APL podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 甚至连一个 APL 播客都没有。

sentences.en: And there is an APL YouTube channel with talks from the dialogue conference that happens once a year.
sentences.zh: 虽然有一个 APL 的 YouTube 频道，里面包含每年举办一次的 dialogue 会议的演讲内容。

sentences.en: But, like, you know, even for a language like Rust, I think there's, like, a handful of Rust conferences, and they typically only last, like, one or two days, whereas C++ has,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，即使对于像 Rust 这样的语言，我想也只有少数的几个 Rust 会议，而且通常只持续一两天，而 C++ 却有，

sentences.en: you know, multiple week-long conferences and just, like, more content than you know what to do with.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，长达数周的会议，内容多到让你应接不暇。

sentences.en: So as a C++ developer –
sentences.zh: 所以作为一名 C++ 开发者——

sentences.en: Fortran has a conference now.
sentences.zh: Fortran 现在也有会议了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Fortran had a conference that – this was their inaugural year, although not a great year to start for an inaugural conference.
sentences.zh: Fortran 举办了一场会议——今年是他们的创办元年，尽管对于一个新创办的会议来说并不是一个太好的年份。

sentences.en: But what are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 但你有什么办法呢？

sentences.en: It's called FortranCon.
sentences.zh: 它叫做 FortranCon。

sentences.en: Yeah, I saw that was in the – we'll add this to the show notes as well.
sentences.zh: 对，我看到那个在——我们也会把它加到节目笔记里。

sentences.en: But in the – on their GitHub page, they have a repo called Talks with all of the slides and talk links linked.
sentences.zh: 但是在他们的 GitHub 页面上，有一个名为 Talks 的仓库，里面链接了所有的幻灯片和演讲链接。

sentences.en: So, yeah, if you find yourself bored and you're interested in either C++ or Fortran or any language, there's tons of content online.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你觉得无聊，并且对 C++、Fortran 或任何语言感兴趣，网上有海量的内容。

sentences.en: And that's where we'll end this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们这一期节目就到这里结束。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening, and we hope you have a great day.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听，希望你们有个美好的一天。
